name: Table Mountain Trail (Standard)
approach: From the Artist Point trailhead (elev. ~5,100 ft, at the end of Mt. Baker Highway/SR 542, GPS approx. 48.847, -121.693) walk to the northwest corner of the large paved parking lot — the signed Table Mountain Trail #681 starts opposite the vault toilets, on the side of the lot away from the highway. The trail begins as a rock-lined gravel path that climbs gently before reaching its first switchback within a few hundred feet. From there the route ascends a tight set of rocky switchbacks blasted directly into the cliff band on Table Mountain's southeast face — this is the crux of the approach: a narrow, exposed catwalk with steep drop-offs toward the Chain Lakes basin and Swift Creek drainage 400-800 ft below. Footing here is loose rock and gravel over hard-packed tread, and snow or verglas frequently lingers in this cliff section into July, making it the most hazardous stretch of the whole route; many parties turn back here in early season without traction devices. After roughly 400 ft of gain (about 0.4-0.5 mi from the car) the switchbacks top out on the broad, relatively flat summit plateau ("the table"). From here follow the well-trodden tread west/northwest along the south rim, which gives open views straight down onto the Chain Lakes Trail; numerous braided use-trails cross the plateau but the main route hugs the south side. At about 1.2 mi you reach the east side of the tabletop with views of Mount Baker and Ptarmigan Ridge, and by 1.3 mi you arrive at two small tarns that frame Mount Shuksan — a natural high point/turnaround for most day hikers and the last easily identified landmark before the trail degrades into a sketchy, unmaintained scramble path descending toward the Table Mountain Glacier. There is no reliable water along the route: the summit tarns are shallow, silty, and not worth treating, so carry all water from the car. Overall to the high point is roughly 1.4-1.5 mi one-way with about 700-725 ft of gain from the trailhead.

approach_variants.name: Table Mountain Trail #681 from the Artist Point lot, up the southeast-face switchbacks
approach_variants.notes:
From the Artist Point trailhead at about 5,100 ft, at the end of the Mount Baker Highway, walk to the northwest corner of the large paved parking lot. Table Mountain Trail #681 starts opposite the vault toilets, on the side of the lot away from the highway.

The trail begins as a rock-lined gravel path and reaches its first switchback within a few hundred feet. From there it climbs a tight set of rocky switchbacks blasted directly into the cliff band on Table Mountain's southeast face — a narrow, exposed catwalk with drops of 400-800 ft toward the Chain Lakes basin and Swift Creek.

After roughly 400 ft of gain, about 0.4-0.5 mile from the car, the switchbacks top out on the broad flat summit plateau. Follow the tread west-northwest along the south rim; braided use-trails cross the plateau but the main route hugs the south side. At about 1.3 miles two small tarns frame Mount Shuksan and mark the usual high point.

There is no water: the tarns are shallow and silty. Carry everything from the car.
approach_variants.season: Roughly Jul-Sep, and it is the road and the snow in the cliff band that decide it rather than the calendar
hazards: An exposed catwalk cut into a cliff band with 400-800 ft drops and loose gravel underfoot
Snow or verglas in the cliff band into July, which is the usual reason parties turn back
Braided use-trails on a flat plateau, the classic place to lose direction in cloud
No water — the summit tarns are shallow and silty
Beyond the tarns the tread degrades into an unmaintained scramble toward the glacier
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The one thing people get wrong here is the trailhead, and it is in a car park. The Artist Point lot is large and paved and has several trails leaving it. Table Mountain Trail #681 starts at the northwest corner, opposite the vault toilets, on the side away from the highway. Three independent descriptors for one gate — corner, toilets, away from the road — which is what you want when the lot is in cloud.

The climbing, such as it is, starts at the first switchback, a few hundred feet in. From there the route is a catwalk cut into the cliff band, and the tread is loose rock and gravel over hard pack with a 400-800 ft drop on the outside.

The cliff band is the crux and also the turnaround point for most early-season parties. Snow or verglas lingers in this section into July, and many parties turn back here without traction devices. That is the honest statement of what this route is: 400 ft of exposed switchback, then a walk.

Arrival on the table: after roughly 400 ft of gain the switchbacks top out on a broad, relatively flat plateau. Flat ground is the confirmation you are through the cliff band.

On the plateau, hug the south rim. Numerous braided use-trails cross the tabletop, and in cloud a plateau with braided paths is the easiest place on this route to end up walking in the wrong direction. The south rim looks straight down onto the Chain Lakes Trail and is the handrail.

Where to stop: the two small tarns at about 1.3 miles are the last easily identified landmark. Beyond them the trail degrades into an unmaintained scramble path descending toward the Table Mountain Glacier. If the path starts going down and gets rough, you have passed the point most parties turn around at.
